5. **Observed, not filed:** in the real console the app shell clears its branding tokens from `html` when the app unmounts, so Studio sits on the default blue. Studio draws graphite over either.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `884c4bd3868b18e95d2da885a99bd8b433125280`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: no

PR #37474, card #37455 (epic #37424). Read: the card's body and its four comments (triage 7184485694, claim 7184943508, the two os-dev reports 7185774932 and 7189264702; no amendment comment exists), the epic's body, ADR-0084's amendment of 2026-11-26 on `main` (PR #37470, merged 10:07Z), the PR body, the final-head comment 7189319006, the net diff against `main` (13 files, +741/−71) and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs on the head: 55 runs, 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. That is 38 distinct names green and 13 skipped; `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` each ran twice (the body refresh). Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, Check PR Size and Governed Surface Queue Guard are among the green.

Findings, graded:

- S1 (should-fix) — the right-slot toggle, the arm drawn when no copilot is served, has no pin in its new home. `studio-slot-toggle` appears in one test only, as a name filtered out of a button list (`saveBar-36511`). Every surface suite doubles the copilot as available, and `studioTitleRow.test.tsx` uses a stub button for the assistant. The browser round did not draw it either. So the area's note 4 and the PR's "their place is pinned by `rightSlot-12725` and `studioTitleRow`" hold for the AI button and not for the toggle. The card's acceptance names the toggle. The code is a verbatim move into the same slot, so I read it as correct; it needs one surface case with the copilot unavailable (toggle in the item header, absent from the top bar, hides and shows the slot).
- S2 (should-fix) — of the five places outside `studio-design/**` that draw the row end, one is pinned. The list hero row is pinned by `rightSlot-12725` ("a list page"). The compact row of `PageShell`, its `!embedded` gate, the directory header and the diagnostics header are not: deleting any of those lines leaves every suite green. The reverse verification restored `PageShell.tsx` but not the other two files. One case each under the surface, plus an embedded control, would hold the deviation the seat is asked to ratify.
- N1 (nit) — the counter in `studioAccent.ts` is right by reading but its counted branch (`mountedSurfaces` above zero on cleanup) has no pin: the graphite suite mounts and unmounts one surface. A plain add/remove would pass the same four cases.
- N2 (nit) — the deviation is described as "one import and one element each". `PageShell.tsx` gets two elements (both rows). `DirectoryPage.tsx` gets one element plus a new flex wrapper and span around the `h1`, which changes that header's markup in Setup too (no visual change expected, nothing drawn there).
- N3 (nit) — `PageShell` passes no `divider` prop, so a list or compact row with no stats and no actions draws the hairline with nothing before it. The item header and the directory header both guard this case.
- N4 (nit) — dark mode has no jsdom pin (the suite reads class scope, which is all jsdom can read). The dark values rest on the Chromium readings in the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

**The top bar against the amendment's table of seven tenants.** This card moves two rows of that table and must leave the other five alone (card: "do not restyle it").

- Save and Cancel → the item header's action slot: right. They end `StudioItemHeader`'s slot after the pillar's own actions and its ⋯ fold. The gate is the old one: the top bar drew them under `!pkgMissing && !allScope`, and `StudioSaveControls` itself returns nothing unless dirty or saving; `titleRowSave` spells the same three conditions.
- Item 6 of the amendment (a page that saves with no item header carries them on its own title row): right, through `StudioTitleRowEnd`. Every `useStudioSaveEntry` caller was traced to a title row: the Data and Automations pillars through `ResourceDetailHeader`, the permission editor through `StudioItemHeader` or its frame's header, the sharing overview through `StudioOwdOverviewPage`'s item header, and the object hooks and pair actions inside the object page. No saving page is left without a Save.
- The AI button and the panel toggle → the right end of each page's title row, behind a hairline: right for the AI button (see S1 for the toggle). The gate is unchanged: `slotHost && slotHasContent`, then `copilotAvailable` picks the arm. The hairline is the same class string as `PageHeader`'s shell divider.
- The way back and its target, the app name, the ⋯ package menu and its rows, Changes and Publish, the menu's show/hide control, and "create app" / "app waits for publish": untouched. The diff has no hunk in `StudioBackToApp.tsx`, `StudioPackageMenu.tsx`, `StudioMenu.tsx` or `studio-tokens.ts`, and the surface's hunks in the header only delete the two moved tenants and reword comments. Order of the remaining tenants is as on `main`.
- Not built here, and not this card's: the two-row top left, the "App Studio" / 应用搭建 label, the switcher, the lock, the rail, the ⋯ rows in 概览's header. At this head the bar still stands and the label still reads as on `main`. Those are #37456, #37454 and the naming card. I name no divergence from the amendment in what this card does build.
- Declared gap, consistent with the amendment's wording ("each page's title row"): a page with no title row draws no assistant. That is the package-not-found state, the pillar-not-found state, loading states, and the permission editor's embedded loading and error shells. The top bar used to show the button there. `⌘.` still works. Once #37456 removes the bar these pages have no visible control for the panel; worth a line on that card.

**Access and visibility.** Nothing is shown to anyone who could not see it before. The controls are built by the surface under the old conditions and only placed by the rows. Outside the surface the context is null and the rows draw nothing (control case in `studioTitleRow.test.tsx`), so Setup's metadata pages gain no button. On the cross-package leg Save stays off (`!allScope`). The ⋯ menu keeps its `canAuthorPackage` gate; no menu row changed.

**The one-owner registry (`studioTitleRow.tsx`).** Right. Rows register in a layout effect, the first in document order owns the controls, and the store is read through `useSyncExternalStore`, so ownership settles before paint. Portalled rows sort after the page, so a sheet cannot take the page's Save. Pinned: nested pair, later row, takeover when the first row goes, no item header, and the outside-surface control.

**The accent scope.** Right.

- Root: `STUDIO_ACCENT` on the `StudioMenuProvider` frame, which wraps the header, the menu, the page and the right slot. The body component has no early return, so the frame and the body hook always go together.
- Body: `useStudioAccentOnBody` is a layout effect with an empty dependency list. Increment and decrement are paired one to one in setup and cleanup. StrictMode runs setup, cleanup, setup: the count ends at 1 and the classes are re-added. A render that throws before commit runs no effect, so it cannot count. An error boundary that unmounts a committed surface runs the cleanup. A Suspense hide destroys and later recreates layout effects, also in pairs. A route swap from one surface to another destroys before it creates in the same commit, and the counter makes either order safe.
- After navigation: the last cleanup removes every class and the marker (pinned, and its ablation is red). The app's inline tokens on the page root are never written, so nothing has to be restored.
- While Studio is mounted the classes on `body` rebind the tokens for everything under `body`, not only Studio's portals. Studio's frame is full-screen, so I see nothing else it could tint. The app's logo keeps its colour: `AppMark` draws from the app's `branding.primaryColor` inline or its own tile palette, not from `--primary`.
- Dark: the `dark:` classes sit on `body`, under the theme class on the page root. The PR's readings give `220 9% 83%` on `body` and on the palette dialog in dark, and a light graphite Save with dark text. See N4.

**Public surface.** None changes. `studioTitleRow.tsx` and `studioAccent.ts` are internal modules of a private package; no export map, schema or metadata key moves.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`, with both declaration lines in the changeset body and the PR body. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes. `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3), so the level is right for a `feat` title too. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `"private": true` and versioned by the changeset config; `Check Changeset` is green.
- The declaration reads `Clause-②: no`, with no arm. Right: the diff moves controls inside one private UI package and adds a class on `body`; no published accept set widens or narrows.
- The changeset text matches the diff, including the portalled surfaces and "Leaving Studio gives the app's pages their own colour back".

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Surface deviation — ratify.** Needed: the amendment's home is "a list's title row, an item's header", and in Studio the list, compact, directory and diagnostics title rows are drawn by `metadata-admin/PageShell.tsx`, `DirectoryPage.tsx` and `DiagnosticsPage.tsx`. No change inside `studio-design/**` could reach them. Minimal: no logic changes, each addition is inert outside the surface. Ratify with N2's corrected description and S2's pins. The forbidden files (`StudioMenu.tsx`, `studio-tokens.ts`) are untouched.
2. **Portal route — accepted.** The counter cannot leak on error or StrictMode and cannot leave the accent on the app's pages; see ① and N1. The dev's alternative (a portal container inside the root) needs `@object-ui/components` and is rightly left out of this card.
3. **Screenshots (N2 of #37478) — taken as reported.** The 14 shots are on the project's card folder, outside this review's inputs; I read the PR body's table of readings and did not open the files.
4. **AI button and toggle not measured in the browser — half answered.** The AI button is pinned in jsdom in both homes. The toggle is not pinned anywhere: S1.
5. **Open question in report 7189264702 (who PATCHes the PR body) — closed.** Comment 7189319006 says the area refreshed the body from the dev's text. Process only, no effect on the diff.
6. **Open question in report 7185774932 (root-only mount or portals too) — settled by the diff as option B**, the `body` class. The dev had recommended A and warned that B "races with the app-branding hook writing root styles". It does not: the hook writes inline styles on the page root and this writes classes on `body`; neither touches the other's node. The changeset and PR body state B plainly.
7. **Out-of-scope notes in the report** (no assistant on rows-less pages; a portal container would retire the body class; the app shell clears its branding on leaving the app) — noted, none blocks. The third means the jsdom case (branding still on the root) is the stricter one, which is the right way round.
8. **SQL push-down** — not applicable: no query, no id materialisation, no join in the diff.


> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
